checks.check: Vitest 5.1 + jsdom 30.1.3: coverage >= 80% with the new include/exclude semantics; port chips/evidence/stream_cut tests
checks.result: PARTIAL: the stack probe PASSES; the read-loop half of the stream_cut port is DONE in I2 on the shipped client; the DOM half and the chips and evidence tests are NOT done (I3)
checks.evidence: 50 tests pass; v8 coverage 100% statements/branches/functions/lines over src with `include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}']` and exclude of components/ui, *.generated.ts, tests and the setup file (the report lists no excluded file); thresholds 80 are set. Probe added 2026-11-07 after the I1 review: web/src/__tests__/smoke-check-6-stream-cut.test.ts, 18 tests, vitest 5.1.0 + jsdom 30.1.3 on Node 24.22.2 (lint and `tsc -b` clean; 75 tests in web/ in all). It runs the pure read-loop half of tests/ui/stream_cut.test.mjs against a stand-in for worker A's `sse.ts` built on the real parser (eventsource-parser 4.1.3): a read that rejects mid-answer, before the first byte and on a real ReadableStream whose second pull errors; a clean end with no done or error; a finished answer or a server error keeping its own status when the stream then ends by a reset or by closing; the ordinary answer; a page failure while an event is taken in (honest status, original error kept, `ended` only once shown); ping comments, unknown events, unknown fields and non-JSON data ignored; a multi-byte character split across chunks; a frame over `maxBufferSize` ends the stream as failed and the terminated parser is not fed again, its next `feed()` throws until `reset()` (confirmed), and without a limit it buffers 200,000 characters (the unbounded default, confirmed). Verdict: the stack hosts the port (TextDecoder, Uint8Array and ReadableStream work across jsdom's realm; the parser's callbacks behave as the types say). Five single-point breaks of the stand-in (no catch around read, no buffer limit, `ended` never set, a page failure reported as a cut, no `stream: true`) were each caught. NOT done: the DOM half of the old tests (statuses written into #status, the Ask button), the response-without-a-body case, and every chips and evidence test; the 16 tests of stream_cut.test.mjs are ported with `sse.ts` in I2 and the components in I3, and the stand-in here is not the shipped client. I2 UPDATE 2026-11-08: the read-loop half is ported onto the shipped client: web/src/lib/__tests__/sse.stream-cut.test.ts runs the 16 cases of tests/ui/stream_cut.test.mjs through askStream (eventsource-parser 4.1.3, MAX_BUFFER_SIZE = 256 KiB), with the response-without-a-body case; the stand-in and its own read loop and 64 KiB placeholder are gone from this probe, which is repointed at askStream and MAX_BUFFER_SIZE and keeps two stack facts (a real ReadableStream whose pull errors is a cut; the parser has no default limit and a 200,000-character frame fits). I3 UPDATE 2026-11-08: the DOM half and the chips and evidence tests are ported; every title of stream_cut.test.mjs (14), chips.test.mjs (12) and evidence.test.mjs (16) has a vitest counterpart (42 titles, each matched by its full title; the verifier found all present) and the full run is green: 61 files, 1113 tests, coverage 98.79/95.57/98.75/99.26, every one of the 70 files at or above 80%, on Node v26.13.0. The result is NOT flipped to PASS yet: that needs a clean full vitest run on Node 24 (CI), which has not happened.

checks.check: Turnstile double-mount under React StrictMode yields one live widget and a fresh token per use
checks.result: PASS as a probe of the stack; the shipped provider and widget run the same cases in web/src/state/__tests__/turnstile.test.tsx (I3, 2026-11-08, green)
checks.evidence: web/src/__tests__/smoke-check-7-turnstile.test.tsx, 7 tests (React 19.3.1, @testing-library/react 16.3.3, jsdom 30.1.3, vitest 5.1.0 on Node 24.22.2; lint and `tsc -b` clean). A fake `window.turnstile` (render, remove, reset, solve, expire; typed in the test, no global declaration) and the smallest hook that follows R33(3): the widget is rendered in an effect with a cleanup that removes it, the token lives in a ref, `consume` clears it and resets the widget, `expired-callback` clears it. Under <StrictMode>: the effect runs twice (2 renders, 1 remove) and exactly one widget stays live, with one frame in the DOM; the same hook with no cleanup leaves two (so the probe is not vacuous); a page change below the shell neither renders nor removes the widget; unmounting leaves none and mounting again leaves one; a token is fresh per use (consume returns it once, clears it, resets the widget; the next solve gives a different token); an expiry clears the token; a late callback of the widget StrictMode discarded does not become the current token. Four single-point breaks (no stale-callback guard, consume keeps the token, expiry ignored, no reset) were each caught. Scope: Cloudflare's real script and the CSP were not exercised (the owner's B6 check), there is no router (a page prop stands in for a route change), and the hook lives in the test file: the shipped hook (src/lib/turnstile*, TurnstileWidget*, I3) must pass the same cases

findings: shadcn 4.23.0 differs from the stack note's prediction: it installs `cn` 0.5.2 (shadcn's own package, MIT, no dependencies) and the components import `cn` from it, instead of clsx + tailwind-merge. clsx stays as a dependency of class-variance-authority; tailwind-merge is not installed. R1's list is completed from this lockfile

shadcn init also added `@fontsource-variable/inter` (OFL-1.1, a web font: out of scope, R4) and `tw-animate-css`; both were removed with `npm uninstall`. The generated `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"` was dropped too: it ships a plain, always-emitted `.shimmer` rule with `animation` (found by the built-CSS scan) and keyframes, and none of the seven components needs its variants

Tailwind v4 turns every word of every scanned file into a candidate class: a code comment containing `transition` made it emit a `.transition` utility (found by the built-CSS scan). The CSS now scans only src (`@import "tailwindcss" source("./")`) and not tests (`@source not`), and carries no such comment

shadcn's seven components (button, badge, card, input, label, table, textarea) had `transition-*` classes, one `translate-y-px` press nudge and a `use client` marker; all stripped (R30). `select` and `skeleton` were NOT installed (a native <select> is used for the strategy and upload-target controls; skeleton animates); `chart` is never installed (HTML sink)

the lockfile has 6 `inBundle` entries (the wasm fallback of @tailwindcss/oxide bundles its runtime) with no resolved/integrity of their own; tests/test_web_pins.py exempts exactly those and checks they sit under a parent entry
